newsitem.title: USA: NHL-THIRTY AN UNLUCKY NUMBER FOR OTTAWA IN CHICAGO SHUTOUT.
newsitem.headline: NHL-THIRTY AN UNLUCKY NUMBER FOR OTTAWA IN CHICAGO SHUTOUT.

text.p: Thirty proved to be an unlucky number for the Senators on Sunday as Ed Belfour recorded a milestone shutout in a 2-0 victory for the Chicago Blackhawks over Ottawa.
Belfour made 24 saves for his 30th career shutout, which trails only Colorado's Patrick Roy among active goaltenders.

"It feels nice. I'm number 30 and that's my 30th shutout," said Belfour, who had gone nearly a year since his last shutout. "I don't know if that means anything or not. Shutouts are never easy. Luck was on my side tonight."
Belfour outdueled Damian Rhodes, who made 23 saves for Ottawa (4-6-5), while Eric Daze and James Black scored to give Chicago their fourth win in five games.
Belfour was rarely tested, but stopped Alexei Yashin's shot through traffic early in the third period and made a glove save on Shawn McEachern's drive during a second-period power play.
"The defence did a great job," said Belfour. "They cleared away the rebounds and they allowed me to see the shots. When I can see the shots, I'm going to make the saves."
The victory allowed Chicago to keep pace with Detroit atop the Atlantic Division with identical 10-6-2 records.

In Detroit, Nicklas Lidstrom broke a 19-game goal-scoring drought and Chris Osgood made 31 saves as the Red Wings spoiled Dino Ciccarelli's return by holding on for a 4-2 win over the slumping Tampa Bay Lightning.
Lidstrom and Vyacheslav Kozlov each had a goal and an assist for the Red Wings, who have lost just once in their last eight home games (6-1-1).
Ciccarellli was playing in Detroit for the first time since the Red Wings traded him to the Lightning last August.
"It was overwhelming," Ciccarelli said of the ovation he received from the fans at Joe Louis Arena. "I didn't expect that, but the fans have been classy my five years here."
Brent Peterson and Patrick Poulin scored for Tampa Bay (6-7-2), winless in eight of their last nine (1-6-2).
In Philadelphia, red-hot John LeClair scored twice, Pat Falloon had a goal and an assist and Ron Hextall made 25 saves to lead the Philadelphia Flyers to a 3-1 victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs.

LeClair's first goal of the game and ninth of the season 9:21 into the second period made it 2-0. He took a drop pass from Karl Dykhuis and blasted a slap shot from the the right faceoff circle past Felix Potvin's glove side.
LeClair, who has scored seven goals in his last four games and has a point on 10 of the last 12 Flyer goals, added a power-play goal with 4:16 remaining in the third.
"I think I'm getting a little more confident around the net," LeClair said. "Right now I'm getting some breaks and some bounces and that's the way it goes."
The Flyers (9-9) won for the fourth time in six games and snapped a three-game home losing streak. Toronto fell to 8-8.
